headline: A US judge has sentenced Michael Smith to 18 months in prison for using AI-made songs and bots to steal more than $8 million in streaming royalties.
score_reason: Lowered by one: the sentencing was on 6 Oct 2026, before the window.
importance_line: Real artists and songwriters lose royalty money to fake streams, and the case shows courts will jail fraudsters, although the 18 months was far below the 46 months prosecutors sought.
summary: Billboard reports that Michael Smith, 54, was sentenced on 6 Oct 2026 in Manhattan federal court to 18 months in prison and two years of supervised release, in what it calls the first criminal case over streaming fraud. He pleaded guilty in March to using AI-generated songs and bots to stream them billions of times for more than $8 million in royalties, which he agreed to forfeit.
notes: Cybernews original blocked and is a rewrite; Billboard reported the sentencing itself, so it is credited and linked.
